Matthew Larn, Director of Recreation and Community Development.
This report seeks City Council's approval to sell approximately 1.2 acres of parkland within Nutana,
Quanna Snorth Park, to Elmwood Residences.
Council first considered Elmwood's request in August of 2024 and referred the matter back to administration for further review.
In August of 2025, administration presented an information report outlined in the process required to evaluate the proposed sale.
Elmwood's current facilities no longer meet its growing needs.
Through the community hub home-based project, Elmwood is proposing a modern, accessible, and inclusive development that integrates health and wellness services,
a range of community supports, and 42 affordable housing units for people living with disabilities, seniors, indigenous peoples, and other priority populations.
Administration has reviewed the proposal and determined that it aligns with several city priorities, including community spaces,
infill development, accessibility and inclusion, health and wellness, affordable housing, economic development, and community-based programming.
To achieve the full vision of this project, Elmwood requires approximately 1.2 acres of land adjacent to its existing facility.
The requested area represents approximately a quarter percent of the total park space within the Nutana sector.
The land currently contains a community garden and several city owned trees.
No operational funding or formal level of service is currently provided for this area.
Administration recognizes the importance of preserving parkland and does not generally support its sale.
However, there is a precedent for this type of arrangement where significant community benefits can be demonstrated,
including the affordable housing project at 1635.
After evaluating their request, Administration is recommending approval of the sale, based on the substantial community benefits the project would provide.
Administration has also identified a suitable area for relocation of the existing community garden, with no loss of planting space or programming opportunities.
All relocation costs, including equivalent infrastructure and site development, would be borne by Elmwood, and would be required to meet city standards.
The gardening collective has been informed of the proposed relocation, and timing would be coordinated to avoid disruptions of the growing season.
The sale would be subject to several conditions outlined in the report and compliant with Section 3.3 of Council Policy, CO90033, sale of city owned lands.
Administration has developed a conditional sale agreement with Elmwood that reflects these requirements.
Pending Council approval, Elmwood intends to finalize design work, obtain approvals, and proceed towards construction.
As required by policy, public engagement was completed in January of 2026.
Feedback was predominantly supportive of the project.
Six participants opposed the proposal, primarily due to concerns about selling parkland to private organizations.
Other feedback focused on traffic, parking, and the relocation of the community garden.
Administration also completed a cost analysis of their request.
The total purchase price in associated costs are $1,707,800.
And this includes fair market value of the land, community garden relocation costs, public engagement costs, and compensation for city trees in accordance with the urban forestry by law.
There would be no cost to the city, and the proceeds from the land sale would be directed to the dedicated lands reserve.
Elmwood would be responsible for all subdivision development and future project related costs.
If Council approves the three report recommendations, administration will work with Elmwood to satisfy all conditions required to complete the sale.

Following completion of the transaction, administration will report back to the Standing Post Seek Committee on Planning Development and Community Service with options to sunset the loss of parkland and order to make improvements to park spaces within the new town of sector.
With that, administration is available to answer any questions.
